reading.summary: In this sample session the S&P 500 edged up about 0.3% and the Nasdaq-100 about 0.6%, led by the large platforms, while software for small merchants sold off hard. The outlets and stories below are invented for the demo.

points.headline: Indices edge higher
points.line: The sample's S&P 500 rose about 0.3% and the Nasdaq-100 about 0.6%; breadth was narrow, with fewer than half the index's members up on the day.

source.title: Closing wrap: a narrow day up (sample)

points.headline: Platforms carry the Nasdaq
points.line: Ledger Street Daily's invented desk credited the large ad and cloud platforms with most of the Nasdaq-100's gain, on what it called relief after last week's selling.

points.headline: Merchant software de-rates
points.line: An invented survey of small merchants in The Tape Desk read softer holiday order books, and the commerce-software names fell the most in the sample session.

points.headline: Brokers bounce
points.line: Retail brokers recovered part of Friday's fall; Harbourline Markets' fictional note pointed to steadier account openings in its own tally.

points.headline: Rating agencies slip
points.line: Data and ratings names gave back some of their October run, which the sample's desk read as profit-taking, not news.

points.headline: Yields little changed
points.line: The sample's ten-year yield ended within two basis points of Monday's close, and the dollar was flat against a basket of currencies.

reading.summary: In this sample session the S&P 500 slipped about 0.5% and the Nasdaq-100 fell about 1.4% as chip stocks extended Friday's fall, while consumer, travel and payments names rose. The outlets and stories below are invented for the demo.

points.headline: Rotation out of chips
points.line: The sample's semiconductor index fell for a second session and the Nasdaq-100 lagged the S&P 500 by almost a point, in a rotation The Tape Desk's invented desk called orderly.

points.headline: Consumer names lead
points.line: Footwear, travel and ride-hailing names led the S&P 500's gainers on what Ledger Street Daily's fictional desk read as a firmer holiday spending outlook.

points.headline: Payments firm
points.line: Card networks rose on the invented Northgate Wire's monthly spending tracker, which it said showed cross-border travel holding up.

points.headline: Latin American commerce rallies
points.line: Regional commerce and fintech names rose as the sample's dollar index eased; Harbourline Markets' fictional note tied it to the currency, not to company news.

points.headline: Brokers extend their fall
points.line: Retail brokers fell again after Friday, the invented desk pointing to lighter trading volumes into the month's end.

points.headline: Defensives mixed
points.line: Utilities and staples were mixed in the sample, and healthcare edged up.

reading.summary: In this sample session the S&P 500 fell about 1.8% and the Nasdaq-100 about 3.5%, its worst day of the month, as chip equipment, brokers and growth software sold off together. The outlets and stories below are invented for the demo.

points.headline: Worst day of the month
points.line: The sample's Nasdaq-100 fell about 3.5% and the S&P 500 about 1.8%; Northgate Wire's invented desk counted four losers for every gainer.

points.headline: Chip equipment leads the fall
points.line: Lithography and deposition names fell the most after an invented note in The Tape Desk argued that orders for next year were already in the price.

points.headline: Brokers drop with volumes
points.line: Retail brokers fell sharply as Harbourline Markets' fictional tally of options volumes dropped from its September high.

points.headline: Growth software sold
points.line: Higher-multiple software names fell with the Nasdaq, the merchant platforms among the weakest in the sample.

points.headline: Defensives hold
points.line: Healthcare and ratings names closed higher, which the invented desk called the session's only shelter.

points.headline: Long yields up
points.line: The sample's ten-year yield rose about six basis points into the weekend.
